nodes.description: PHOST is a distinctive, unencapsulated mesenchymal lesion found in PHTS, including BRRS presentations. Mature adipose and fibrous or myxoid tissue are intermixed with abnormal veins, thick-walled arteries, small vessels, and occasional arteriovenous communications. It commonly infiltrates muscle, fascia, and subcutis and may cause pain and swelling. It is one of several PHTS-associated vascular/connective tissue lesions, not a synonym for all vascular malformations.

nodes.description: Genotype combinations test cell-autonomous and cross-cell effects on phagocytosis and synaptic-marker abundance. nodes.description: Renal cell carcinoma occurs in the PTEN spectrum, including papillary histology. The often-cited 34% lifetime estimate comes from older PHTS data and should not be read as a BRRS-specific risk or a universally accepted estimate.

evidence.snippet: The lifetime risk for renal cell cancer (predominantly of papillary histology) is 34%.

nodes.description: Sirolimus (rapamycin) is the lesion-directed mTOR-inhibitor use in BRRS, distinct from the neurocognitive indication that the everolimus trial tested and missed. It is used off-label for symptomatic vascular anomalies when other treatments have failed, and the BRRS-specific published experience is a single pediatric case in the 2024 systematic review. Evidence is therefore anecdotal, and this is curated as an off-label option under investigation rather than standard care.

nodes.description: Everolimus targets the mTOR overactivity that follows PTEN loss, giving a direct mechanistic rationale. A 6-month phase II randomized placebo-controlled trial in 46 individuals with PHTS (eligible ages 5 to 45 years) found the drug tolerable but did not meet its primary neurocognitive endpoint, with gastrointestinal adverse events more common on treatment. mTOR inhibition therefore remains investigational for the neurodevelopmental features of BRRS and is not routine care.
